messages.subject: error message
parts:
Hello:

 

I have been using lavaan for over four years now and I don’t usually have a problem.

 

Recently, I tried to use lavaan to test a theoretical model and I ran into difficulties. To be specific, I reviewed the relevant literature (mostly from cross-sectional surveys) and did a meta-analysis for each path in the theoretical model. This gave me estimates of the correlations among all the variables specified in the model. I then used these correlations (and the harmonic mean of the N’s for each meta-analysis) as data for a SEM using lavaan to specify the theoretical model and to run the analysis using the sem() function. Although there was no problem when I inputted the correlations matrix and specified the model, the analysis did not run. Instead RStudio gave me the following error message.:

 

Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :

  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘Summary’ for

signature ‘"lavaan"’

 

Does anyone know what this error message means and how I might circumvent it?

 

Thanks, Peter

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: error message
parts: > unable to find an inherited method for function ‘Summary’ for signature ‘"lavaan"’

Did you type "Summary"? It should be "summary", all lower case.

By the way, not related to lavaan but related to meta-analysis. Have you thought about using metaSEM to do the meta-analysis? I understood it was common to use harmonic mean or some other methods to get a "sample size" to do meta-analytic structural equation modeling (MASEM). However, other methdos, such as two-stage SEM, are theoretically more defensible in doing MASEM. For example, instead of trying to find a number ("sample size") to represent the sampling error, TSSEM directly estimates the sampling error:

This can be done by metaSEM:

https://cran.r-project.org/package=metaSEM

A lot of features have been added since 2015 but the following paper may still be good paper to give you an idea of the approach, using the package for illustration:

Cheung, M. W.-L. (2015). metaSEM: An R package for meta-analysis using structural equation modeling. Frontiers in Psychology, 5(January), 1–7. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2014.01521

Chapter 7 of the following book also introduces the TSSEM approach:

Cheung, M. W. L. (2015). Meta-analysis: A structural equation modeling approach. John Wiley & Sons, Inc.

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: b841a29904b5c06c
messages.subject: Re: error message
parts:
Thanks everyone for your help, especially Shu Fai. Your reply solved the problem.

Hi Shu Fai:

Thanks very much for your suggestions. I really like MASEM and I have the book you reference.  I also did Mike Cheung's  online, 3 day workshop this January which I highly recommend.

I also like the following two articles:

Jak, S. & Cheung, M. W-L. (2020). Meta-analytic structural equation modeling with moderating effects on SEM parameters. Psychological Methods, 25(4), 430–455. http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000245

Jak, S., Li, H., Kolbe, L., de Jonge, H., & Cheung, MW-L. (2021). Meta‐analytic structural equation modeling made easy: A tutorial and web application for one‐stage MASEM. Research Synthesis Methods, 12(5), 590-606. https://doi.org/10.1002/jrsm.1498

I did do MASEM using the metaSEM package for the core theoretical model as the effects sizes (correlations) are based upon a relatively large number of studies. 

However, some of the paths in the full theoretical model have not been studied very much and the effect sizes for some of these peripheral paths are only based upon a few studies.
When I try to to use metaSEM for the  full theoretical model, then the package cannot handle the large amount of missing data when estimating the peripheral paths (the solution is unstable). This is why I am using a univariate (old fashioned) approach and the harmonic mean to test the full theoretical model.

All the best,

Peter
